text.content: Granddaughter of a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} prince and daughter of a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} archon, Jezebelle joined the crusade to retake New York hoping to prove herself worthy of her lineage after the mass @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} exodus from the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} left the clan's remaining members under suspicion. Leading a ferocious strike pack, she distinguished herself in the Bronx raid and the final assault on Archbishop Polonia's stronghold, fighting alongside Theo Bell and earning Prince Calebros' personal commendation at the post-battle conclave. Tragically, nearly every elder who witnessed her heroics has since left the city, and the neonates who remain have no interest in celebrating a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}'s glory over their own; Jezebelle now finds herself an unrecognized hero in a city that has already forgotten the war she helped win.

pages.name: Hester Reed, Ductus of Love's Easy Tears

text.content: A product of late-1970s New York punk nightlife, Hester Reed was Embraced by a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} addicted to sharing her heroin-fueled highs after she overdosed in his Chelsea Hotel haven. She rose to become ductus of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} pack Love's Easy Tears, served occasionally as a templar to Archbishop Polonia, and led her pack through the doomed six-night stand against the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s 1999 counteroffensive, losing most of her packmates to @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Justicar Cock Robin and archon Federico di Padua. Rather than flee with Polonia, Hester kept her pack's tattered remains in New York, and now wages a campaign of psychologically brutal, rarely lethal ambushes against individual Kindred and small coteries — terror tactics meant to slow the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s consolidation while she and her two surviving packmates seek new recruits to rebuild Love's Easy Tears into a force that matters again.

Embraced in 1891 by the itinerant @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} violinist Tamoszius Kuszleika, who abandoned her in New York rather than face the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}, Yvette has spent much of her unlife in torpor, mourning a deaf mortal man she fell for but could never find a way to reach. She is, unknowingly, a hidden thread in one of New York's deepest secrets: it was Yvette who followed a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} mob to their Palla Grande decades ago and, on impulse, dragged the fallen bishop Ecaterina to safety after an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} antitribu assassination attempt — not realizing the Cainite she saved now walks the city's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} circles as Katherine Wiese. Only Yvette's total disconnection from Kindred politics has kept her from ever recognizing the face she once rescued.

pages.name: Masika St. John, the Camnet Innovator

text.content: A young @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} apprentice who theorized that computers function as mental extensions of their users and are therefore susceptible to Thaumaturgical manipulation, Masika St. John developed the rudiments of an entirely new Path of Technomancy in 1998 and disseminated her theories across an Internet backbone she built among fellow apprentices herself — a feat of innovation unmatched by any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} apprentice in over a century. Threatened by her success, her original regent had her reassigned to New York's Kenilworth chantry under the notoriously conservative Lord Ephraim Wainwright, who despises her “bastard sorcery” on principle. Masika endures his hostility with the support of a few sympathetic young @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, and some conspiratorially minded Kindred whisper that her discovery may have been quietly catalyzed by an unseen Methuselah's influence rather than her own genius alone.

pages.name: Thomas Arturo, Harpy and Haven Designer

text.content: A @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} architect and interior designer whose services became indispensable as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s victorious Kindred rebuilt New York's havens and Elysia, Thomas Arturo has parlayed his exclusive clientele — among them the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}'s Maupassant Room and fellow harpy Hellene Panhard's penthouse — into a social gravity usually reserved for primogen. He reserves his favor for the traditional @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}-@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}-@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} power bloc, holds a rare mutual respect for Calebros, and has taken an interest in the disturbed @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} Adelaide Davis, fully aware of and intending to eventually exploit her history of killing children.

pages.name: Hellene Panhard, the Harpy Who Owns Boss Callihan

text.content: A well-placed @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} harpy with contacts throughout New York's import trade, Hellene Panhard uncovered Boss Callihan's plot to have an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} assassinate the ascending Prince Calebros in the chaotic weeks after the Battle of New York. Rather than exposing the anarch boss and risking the appearance of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} disorganization at a fragile moment, Panhard intercepted the assassin, interrogated him, and quietly confronted Callihan directly — extracting a Blood Bond from him in exchange for her silence. She now holds one of the anarch movement's most prominent leaders as a secret, devoted thrall, a leash she has yet to use for any purpose beyond her own amusement and information-gathering.

A Kindred card sharp who runs a Friday-night high-stakes card game that has become an informal neutral ground for New York's Kindred, Nicky the Chop is secretly the alternate identity of a Cainite named Diana, who appears before New York's Kindred in both guises without anyone suspecting the connection. Regulars treat the game as an unofficial Elysium where politics are left at the door, but a disproportionate number of anarchs have begun attending, worrying Diana that she may be perceived as an anarch sympathizer — and, more dangerously, that mortal organized crime may soon come looking for a cut of her profitable little operation.

vtmlarp.source: New York by Night, 2nd Edition, Chapters Two and Three
